\chapter{Bring It Over: The Food Counter's Own Word}
\label{ch:mw-bring-request}
\hlchaptermodality{30}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can order any of the seven food words this book has taught, and tell the five asking words apart by the job each one does.}

The asking word a food counter needs arrives by ear, joins a food noun in the shortest complete sentence this track writes, and the five asking words taught so far are then separated by job in four separately scored skills.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[lāvo]{Hear \emph{lāvo} — bring it}

\label{lesson:MW-C25-hear-lavo}



\begin{quote}
Recall the closing payoff and the three-word transport payoff, then write bus and \emph{make it}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{lāvo} — \textbf{bring it}
\end{quote}

Two beats, and the fourth asking word in this track. Say them in the order you met them: \emph{dikhāvo}, \emph{karo}, \emph{lo}, \emph{do}, \emph{lāvo}. Every one ends the same way.

\emph{lāvo} is the one a food counter needs. You do not ask for tea to be shown to you; you ask for it to be brought. The source prints it with a food word, which is exactly where the next lesson puts it.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[lāvo]{\mw{लावो} — bring it, on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C25-lavo}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{bring it}, then write wind and \emph{show it}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ला}} + \textbf{\mw{वो}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{लावो}} — \emph{lāvo} — bring it
\end{quote}

Three signs, none new. Its ending \textbf{\mw{वो}} is the same one that closes \textbf{\mw{दिखावो}}. Write \textbf{\mw{लो}} and \textbf{\mw{लावो}} one under the other: same first letter, and everything after it is what separates taking from bringing.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look at the pair, cover it, wait five seconds, and write both from their meanings: first \emph{take it}, then \emph{bring it}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[chāy lāvo]{Hear \emph{chāy lāvo} — bring tea}

\label{lesson:MW-C25-hear-bring-request}



\begin{quote}
Recall the seven-word food payoff, say the request from Chapter 26, then write the sweet crumbled wheat dessert, tea, and \emph{bring it}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{chāy lāvo} — \textbf{bring tea}
\end{quote}

Two words. The food comes first and the asking word last, the same order you already use in \emph{ye kapṛā dikhāvo}, with the pointing word left out because you are not choosing between cups in front of you.

Any of the seven food words fits the first slot. Say the line three times, with \emph{chāy}, then \emph{roṭī}, then \emph{dāl}, and notice that nothing else in it moves.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[chāy lāvo.]{\mw{चाय} \mw{लावो।} — the order on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C25-bring-request}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{ट}}, then write flatbread and hard wheat rolls.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{चाय} | \mw{लावो।}}
\end{quote}

Two written words and a stop. Now write the same line twice more, replacing \textbf{\mw{चाय}} with \textbf{\mw{रोटी}} and then with \textbf{\mw{बाटी}}. Only the first word changes, and you have written all three of those words before.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read the line once. Cover it for ten seconds and write it. Then write the two variants from memory and check that \textbf{\mw{लावो}} is identical in all three.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieve \emph{bring it} against the other four}

\label{lesson:MW-R25-bring-two}



\begin{quote}
Write \emph{very} and \emph{a little}, then say which one makes a description stronger.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Five asking words are now in play. Hear them shuffled and give each meaning. Read five cards: \textbf{\mw{दिखावो}}, \textbf{\mw{करो}}, \textbf{\mw{लो}}, \textbf{\mw{दो}}, \textbf{\mw{लावो}}. Write all five from sound, then write the tea order and say which of the five it uses.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}; \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Payoff — five asking words, five jobs}

\label{lesson:MW-C25-request-five}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-counter request payoff and write the request itself.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
All five end in the same sound and none of them is interchangeable.

1. Hear all five shuffled and name each one's job. 2. Produce all five from their jobs alone, without the sounds. 3. Read five cards and match each to one line you already know. 4. Write all five from dictation, then write the tea order, the counter-offer, and the closing question that asks for a final price.

Pass each skill separately. Five ways to ask is not five ways to be understood: refusing, thanking somebody for doing it, and asking again more softly are all still untaught.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}; \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Close the writing loop for \mw{ल}, \mw{व} and \mw{च}}

\label{lesson:MW-R25-script-close}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word asking payoff, then write child and wind.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Write five single signs from sound cues: \textbf{\mw{ल}}, \textbf{\mw{व}}, \textbf{\mw{च}}, \textbf{\mw{छ}}, \textbf{\mw{ख}}. Two of those five are breathed partners of the two before them; say all five and mark which two carry the breath.

Then write \textbf{\mw{लावो}}, \textbf{\mw{लो}}, \textbf{\mw{दिखावो}}, \textbf{\mw{चाय} \mw{लावो।}}, and \textbf{\mw{पाछे} \mw{मिलसू}} from dictation. Repair only the missed sign and rewrite its word once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}; \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
